title: Intel Windows Vulkan ray-query and TLAS tests abort depending on GPUAV configuration
body:
On source-clean upstream 60cef2be828e03ba54e2e1598001b4625c0c2163, unchanged registry gpu-allocator/lock and none of our wgpu PR patches, two Vulkan tests abort with GPU-based validation enabled and pass in three matched trials each with GPUAV removed:

- wgpu_gpu::binding_array::tlas::binding_array_tlas
- wgpu_gpu::ray_tracing::shader::prevent_invalid_ray_query_calls

Platform: Windows / Intel Arc integrated graphics; Vulkan SDK 1.4.363.0. The evidence includes exact adapter/configuration receipts. A test-initialization-only harness controls the flag because the tests request GPUAV explicitly: environment-only attempts did not disable it. Each mode uses the same executable bytes, basename, directory, working directory, adapter and metadata; core validation remains enabled. Every process asserts and prints its final flags, and layer warnings confirm the on-mode setting. Three trials interleave mode order. All six on executions abort; all six off executions pass.

Reproduce by applying historical/pressure-recovery-20261128/sources/gpuav-flag-control-harness.patch to the pinned upstream revision, then running either named test with the harness control on/off. The source, commands, all logs and JUnit are in the evidence bundle's GPUAV_CONTROL.md and gpuav-flag-controls directory. An earlier off-only pilot's first TLAS run timed out at 90 seconds; subsequent runs passed, and that timeout is retained.

This establishes configuration dependence, not whether the fault is validation instrumentation, shader/driver interaction or another component. Off-mode runs change the test's requested configuration and are diagnostic results, not conformance passes. No production workaround or allocator attribution is proposed. Current trunk bfa9aff differs from the pinned control only in CI dependency updates, not runtime source.

Agent-assisted investigation and report. Evidence: https://github.com/simzy39/winit-wgpu-repro-benchmarks/tree/main/allocator-reconciliation-20261128
